why_this_window: The first committed S2 window that contains a 1-up jingle and its restore. The window opens at a ROM epoch and not at a hand-chosen frame: row 20107 is the service on which zCurSong becomes 82h, the level music load, with zAbsVar.1upPlaying already zero because zPlayMusic's .bgmnot1up branch clears it on an ordinary load (s2.sounddriver.asm:1728-1731). MusID_ExtraLife (98h, s2.constants.asm:856) is requested on the service ending row 22991, where zPlayMusic backs up zAbsVar and every track into zTracksSaveStart and sets 1upPlaying to 80h (s2.sounddriver.asm:1675-1724). cfFadeInToPrevious runs on the service ending row 23201, restoring the region and fading the level music back in (s2.sounddriver.asm:3083-3163). The window carries 399 further services so the whole 28h-step fade-in is inside it. zCurSong stays 98h across the restore because it lives at 1300h, outside the backed-up zAbsVar region, so the song byte is not evidence of the restore; 1upPlaying is.
epoch: Level music load. Tick 0 is the service on which zCurSong = 82h and 1upPlaying = 00h.
rom_restore_contract: Measured at tick 3085 and stated by cfFadeInToPrevious (s2.sounddriver.asm:3083-3163). Every playing FM and PSG music track carries PlaybackControl bit 1 -- track at rest (:3107, :3131). The DAC track carries PlaybackControl bit 2, the SFX-overriding bit the routine sets so the DAC stays silent through the fade (:3094). Track volumes carry the 28h - FadeInCounter attenuation (:3098-3099, :3109, :3134). zAbsVar.FadeInFlag is 80h and FadeInCounter is 28h (:3151-3153), and 1upPlaying is back to 00h (:3155). The next service, tick 3086, already shows FadeInCounter 27h with every track volume one lower, so the first fade step is immediate.
sampling: driver RAM 12FEh..2000h captured by the observer core as a completion snapshot on the driver's own service boundaries, identical in shape and bounds to the committed w10150-12400 and CPZ references.

observer.core_provenance: The core was not rebuilt for this capture. The build the widen lane produced was checked against artifact-lock.json on all four values -- compressed digest, decompressed digest, build id and observer identity -- before use, and installed beside the stock distribution.

window_discovery: The 1-up was located by a chunked driver-state sweep of the whole 259593-row recording that reduced each chunk to the transitions of zCurSong (1300h) and zAbsVar.1upPlaying (1B91h) and then discarded the payload. Nine 1-up jingles occur in the recording; this is the first whose restore returns to level music that is still loaded, rather than being followed immediately by a new music load.
